10.title: Vault
10.content:
×

“The Vaults were nothing more than a hole in the ground for rich folks to hide in while the rest of the world burned.”— [Ma June](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Ma_June "Ma June")

A **Vault** is a type of survival shelter designed to protect individuals from nuclear war.[[1]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-1) Leaders who managed Vaults are known as [overseers](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Overseer "Overseer").

Background
----------

Vault-Tec built over 100 Vaults,[[2]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-2) sometimes numbered at specifically 122,[[3]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-3) around the [United States](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/United_States "United States") and [Canada](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Canada "Canada")[[4]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-4) as part of the [Societal Preservation Program](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Societal_Preservation_Program "Societal Preservation Program"). The company also sponsored an exhibit at the [Museum of Technology](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Museum_of_Technology "Museum of Technology") in Washington D.C., designed to promote their shelters and explain their functionality.[[5]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-5) Not all Vaults were completed by the Great War, and some Vaults sealed without many of their intended inhabitants, while other Vaults were constructed in secret, their numbers omitted from public record.[[6]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-6)

The [Series 1000 Shelter](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Series_1000_Shelter "Series 1000 Shelter") was an alternative offered by Vault-Tec, for those too long of a distance from a Vault.[[Pub 1]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-series-7) The Series 1000 was a one-level subterranean mini-Vault priced for a small corporation or medium-sized community.[[Pub 1]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-series-7)[Fallout shelters](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Fallout_Shelter_(Fallout_Television_Series) "Fallout Shelter (Fallout Television Series)") were also available for residential locations.[[7]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-8)

Despite the Societal Preservation Program's noble goals, a secretive shadow government subverted the project in order to preserve specific portions of society for secretive reasons within the 17 control Vaults. According to rumors, these elements would go on to cause or quicken the [Great War](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Great_War "Great War") in order to see their vision made reality, and their plans continue through the actions of the [Enclave](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Enclave "Enclave").[[8]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-Enclave-9)

“Thanks to a generous grant from the Vault-Tec corporation, the Vault Tour is open to the public. Walk through a section of actual Vault and observe all of the modern conveniences Vault-Tec has added to its now legendary nuclear fallout shelters. Interact with the exhibits within the Vault and see just how life within one of these subterranean marvels is as comfortable as living at home. Time tickets for the tour are now available at the Information Desk in the Main Atrium.”— [Museum of Technology](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Museum_of_Technology_Terminal_Entries "Museum of Technology Terminal Entries")

“_A Vault-Tec Vault is a vast wonderful place, not made by God almighty but by the working man. A veritable Camelot of the nuclear age! Residents are safe underground behind three-foot thick led casing — strong enough to keep out the rads and the reds! And best of all, each underground burg comes with all the modern amenities you come to expect from our rip-roaring Republic. No matter what comes our way, America will be ready._”— [Cooper Howard](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Cooper_Howard "Cooper Howard")

### Vault Life

Vault life varies depending on whether the residents are in one of the 17 control Vaults[[9]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-10), or in one of the 105 experimental Vaults.[[10]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-11) To apply for a spot in a Vault, potential candidates were required to fill out the following forms: GZ089 Health Form, TR17 Liability Waiver, LM222 Last Will and Testament Form, DB104 Vault-Tec Citizenship Agreement, XM003 Organ Donation Invoice, HW660 Psychological Evaluation Screening, KY269 Intimate Relations Conduct Agreement, PLK575 Rights Revocation Charter and the FQS010 Family History Form.[[11]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-12) Vault-Tec gave out awards to dwellers and trophies are displayed in residential areas. Awards granted to Vault Dwellers included those for the Annual Halloween Costume Contest, Vault Dweller of the Year, Excellence in Bravery, Performance Award for Vault Hall Monitors, Cleanest Toilet, Best Looking Hair, and Outstanding Achievement.[[12]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-13)

Vault-Tec provided all clothing, bedding, and accommodations for residents. Personal belongings had to be reviewed and approved of by an authorized Vault-Tec hermetics technician before belongings could be delivered to reserved quarters within a Vault. In the event of an emergency entrance, no personal belongings were permitted beyond the main door of the facility.[[13]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-VT_letter-14) Vault 101 inhabitants were given ration coupons.[[14]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-15) Inhabitants were required to place their trash into incineration receptacles on scheduled burning days.[[15]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-16) Deceased dwellers are also incinerated.[[16]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-17)

To maintain the health of inhabitants, [Auto-Docs](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Auto-Doc "Auto-Doc") were installed in Vaults.[[17]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-18)[Atmospheric Contaminant Detection](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Atmospheric_Contaminant_Detection "Atmospheric Contaminant Detection") systems were installed at the entryway of some Vaults. The average life expectancy of a resident in a properly maintained Vault was 92.3 years.[[18]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-19)

The living sections used the [Floorsuck Autocleaner System](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Floorsuck_Autocleaner_System "Floorsuck Autocleaner System") to maintain floor cleanliness.[[19]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-20) The [Culinator 3000 Kitchen System](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Culinator_3000_Kitchen_System "Culinator 3000 Kitchen System") was installed for cooking.[[20]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-21)[SimuSun Lighting](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/SimuSun_Lighting "SimuSun Lighting") mimicked the feeling of being outside, and the [Entertainotron Room](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Entertainotron_Room "Entertainotron Room") was a "Vault-Tec innovation" provided to residents wishing to watch holotapes or listen to a symphony.[[21]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-22)[[22]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-23) Vaults were installed with [Vault Ceiling Sprinklers](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault_Ceiling_Sprinklers "Vault Ceiling Sprinklers") as a fire suppression mechanism and underwent a Vault-Tec radiation proofing inspection.[[23]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-24)

### Vault Jumpsuits

Vault Dwellers were provided the suits upon entry to the Vault.[[25]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-26) Locations such as [Vault 111](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault_111 "Vault 111") contained boxes of ten jumpsuits.[[26]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-27)[[27]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-28) Members of the [Enclave](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Enclave "Enclave") on the [presidential rig](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Control_Station_ENCLAVE "Control Station ENCLAVE") wore Vault suits.[[28]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-29) Some Vault suits were made of extruded rubber, while others are made of leather and sold as souvenirs after the war.[[29]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-30)[[30]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-31)[[31]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-32) Vault suits were created with their location's number on the back, except for those worn by citizens of [Vault City](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault_City "Vault City").[[32]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-33)[[33]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-34) Some inhabitants were given [Pip-Boys](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Pip-Boy "Pip-Boy").[[34]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-35)[[35]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-36) In [Vault 101](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault_101 "Vault 101"), they were given when a child turned 10.[[36]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-37)

Construction
------------

[![Image 46: S1E8 World Object 4.jpg](https://images.fallout.wiki/thumb/5/5c/S1E8_World_Object_4.jpg/250px-S1E8_World_Object_4.jpg)](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/File:S1E8_World_Object_4.jpg)

[Eye-On-You Cameras](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Eye-On-You_Camera "Eye-On-You Camera") were used for security.[[37]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-38) The [Vault 101 PA System](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault_101_PA_System "Vault 101 PA System") advertised that Vault-Tec water and life support systems sustain Vaults for over 900 years without failure.[[38]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-39)[[39]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-40) Some Vaults were installed with [GECKs](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/GECK "GECK").[[40]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-41) The structural integrity of Vaults were designed to last generations.[[41]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-42) The interiors were stated to be outfitted with Triple-S Technology, or "the three most important parts of apocalyptic endurance:Safety, Survivability and Sanitation!"[[42]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-43)

### Doors

![Image 47: >> ](https://images.fallout.wiki/thumb/9/9c/Hat_arrow.png/24px-Hat_arrow.png)

Vault blast doors were designed to protect from nuclear fallout.[[Pub 2]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-44) The doors had a projected 2% failure rate in case of a direct hit by an atomic bomb.[[43]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-45)[[44]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-46) Different variants of the door included the Seal-N-Safe model No. 343 that measured four feet in thickness, constructed with steel, and contained twelve cogs, used in the [demonstration Vault](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/The_Cathedral "The Cathedral").[[45]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-47)[[Pub 3]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-48) Specific access codes are necessary to operate some doors, while other panels require connection to a Pip-Boy to access the door controls.[[46]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-49) The [Vault City](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault_City "Vault City") doors are built with power couplings.[[47]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-50)

### Vault Experiments

Some Vaults had a unique set of circumstances designed to test the occupants, such as not having enough food synthesizers, only men, or opening after only six months.[[48]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-testprez-51) Scientists at the [Hawthorne Medical Laboratories](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Hawthorne_Medical_Laboratories "Hawthorne Medical Laboratories"), a Vault-Tec division, attempted to create hybrid humans in [Vault 4](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault_4 "Vault 4") using radioactive resistant species, the result of which was the [Gulper](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Gulper_(Fallout_Television_Series) "Gulper (Fallout Television Series)").[[49]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-52)

Notes
-----

*   In the [Vault-Tec Headquarters](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault-Tec_Headquarters "Vault-Tec Headquarters"), a Vault door can be seen hanging from the ceiling to the right of the lobby.
*   In the main hall of the [Vault-Tec University](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault-Tec_University "Vault-Tec University"), there is an unnumbered Vault door displayed.
*   In _[Fallout Shelter](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Fallout\_Shelter "Fallout Shelter")_, players choose their own Vault's number, and players are sent to various Vault [locations](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Fallout_Shelter_locations "Fallout Shelter locations").
*   [John-Caleb Bradberton](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/John-Caleb_Bradberton "John-Caleb Bradberton") lives in a Vault underneath [Nuka-Town USA](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Nuka-Town_USA "Nuka-Town USA").
*   Several Vaults appear in the _[Bethesda Pinball](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Bethesda\_Pinball "Bethesda Pinball")_ game, including Vault 33, 41, 66, 99, 103, 107, and 113.

Appearances
-----------

Vaults appear across the [Fallout Series](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Overview:Fallout_Series "Overview:Fallout Series").

Behind the Scenes
-----------------

*   [Tim Cain](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Tim_Cain "Tim Cain"), [Leonard Boyarsky](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Leonard_Boyarsky "Leonard Boyarsky"), and [Jason D. Anderson](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Jason_D._Anderson "Jason D. Anderson") first came up with the idea of Vaults housing dark experiments during the initial development stages of _Fallout 2_, with the more "wacky" experiments being developed after the three left Interplay.[[Dev 1]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-53)
*   Vaults are mentioned in the [Fallout Bible](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Fallout_Bible "Fallout Bible").[[Dev 2]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-54)[[Dev 3]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-55)
*   According to [Chris Taylor](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Chris_Taylor "Chris Taylor"), the Master's Vault was built as a demonstration model for the federal government, and was close to Vault-Tec's headquarters.[[Dev 4]](https://fallout.wiki/wiki/Vault#cite_note-56)

11.content:
What follows is a complete **timeline** of all known canonical events in the _Fallout_ universe.

For clarity and performance, some parts of the timeline were separated into other articles:

The [_Fallout_ world](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Fallout_world "Fallout world") is not our own. It is set in a universe that [diverged](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Divergence "Divergence"), but shares many historical milestones prior to the events of World War II:[\[Non-game 1\]](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_note-1)[\[Non-game 2\]](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_note-2) While it takes place in the future, it is not our future, but one reflecting a traditional 1950s-style science fiction "world of tomorrow."[\[Non-game 3\]](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_note-3)

In _Fallout 76_, [Professor Greebly](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Greebly "Greebly") postulates the existence of multiple timelines.[\[859\]](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_note-1048)

1.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-4) The [Sole Survivor](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Sole_Survivor "Sole Survivor"): _"That's really interesting."_  
    [Jack Cabot](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Jack_Cabot "Jack Cabot"): _"I'm glad to hear you say that. It's become my life's work. My approach is to combine a rigorous scientific method while keeping an absolutely open mind. So much has been closed off to us simply because people assumed they already knew the answers. My father excavated a city in the Rub'al Khali in Arabia which he dated to more than 4,000 years before the rise of any known human civilization. The structures and artifacts were... strange. Disturbing, even. Clearly not constructed for or by humans. I've spent my life trying to decipher what he uncovered."_  
    ([Jack Cabot's dialogue](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/JackCabot.txt "JackCabot.txt"))
2.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-5) [Pioneer Scout camp terminal entries; pioneer badge exam terminal, tadpole exams, archer](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Pioneer_Scout_camp_terminal_entries#Archer "Pioneer Scout camp terminal entries")
3.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-6) [Edwin Brotch](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Edwin_Brotch "Edwin Brotch"): _"No, Mister DeLoria, that is not correct. The Battle of Hastings was 1066. 2077 was the end of the world. Tell me. Are you really that stupid?"_  
    ([MrBrotch.txt](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/MrBrotch.txt "MrBrotch.txt")) **Note:** Heard during the transition between 10 and 16 years during the vault sequence.
4.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-7) Toshiro Kago was abducted sometime during the Tokugawa shogunate, starting on March 24, 1603, since _mon_ were only authorized for all classes from that date.
5.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-8) The [Lone Wanderer](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Lone_Wanderer "Lone Wanderer"): _"That's quite an unusual name."_  
    Fawkes: _"It was taken from a historical entry in the computer. The name comes from a man who was willing to fight and die for what he believed in. I felt it was appropriate given my circumstances."_  
    ([Fawkes' dialogue](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/MQ08Fawkes.txt "MQ08Fawkes.txt"))
6.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-9) [Coastal monument](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Coastal_monument "Coastal monument") plaque: _"Here marks the landing of Captain John Smith's shallop upon his discovery of Point Lookout in 1612."_
7.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-10) The [Sole Survivor](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Sole_Survivor "Sole Survivor"): _"I'm ready."_  
    [Parker Quinn](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Parker_Quinn "Parker Quinn"): _"Every day, you gotta buy stuff. Food, ammo, beer, whatever. And you pay with caps. Caps. Bottle caps. What is this, fuckin' 1612? A bunch of losers blow up the world 200 years ago, and we have to lug around piles of bottle caps. Are you friggin' kidding me? So that's why I've been working with every single shop in the Commonwealth to get RID of caps."_  
    ([Nate's](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/MQDadVoice.txt "MQDadVoice.txt")/[Nora's](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/MQMomVoice.txt "MQMomVoice.txt") and [Parker Quinn's dialogue](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/ParkerQuinn.txt "ParkerQuinn.txt"))
8.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-11) [_Point Lookout_ loading screens](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Fallout_3_loading_screens#Point_Lookout "Fallout 3 loading screens"): _"The Ark & Dove Cathedral is named for two English settler ships which landed near Point Lookout in 1634, leading to Maryland's founding."_
9.  ↑ [9.0](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-OGBG_12-0) [9.1](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-OGBG_12-1) _[Fallout 4 Vault Dweller's Survival Guide](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Fallout_4_Vault_Dweller%27s_Survival_Guide "Fallout 4 Vault Dweller's Survival Guide")_ Collector's Edition p.472: _"**\[14.02\] Old Granary Burying Ground**_  
    _This burial ground was established in 1660, making it the oldest surviving burial ground in Boston. Many famous Revolutionary War heroes were buried here, including John Hancock, Paul Revere, Samuel Adams, and the victims of the Boston Massacre. In 2031, after the tragic death of Emilia Butler, the city council voted unanimously to have her remains interred here._  
    _This is part of the Freedom Trail. The number “2” is daubed on the circular ground plaque pointing at the letter “A.” It is overrun by ferals. The adjacent church is sealed and cannot be entered."_  
    ([Fallout 4 Vault Dweller's Survival Guide Map](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Fallout_4_Vault_Dweller%27s_Survival_Guide_Map "Fallout 4 Vault Dweller's Survival Guide Map"))
10.  ↑ [10.0](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-PaulRevereHouseInscription_13-0) [10.1](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-PaulRevereHouseInscription_13-1) [Paul Revere House inscription](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Boston_landmark_inscriptions#Paul_Revere_House "Boston landmark inscriptions")

[↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-14) [_Fallout 4_ loading screens](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Fallout_4_loading_screens#CityDiamondCity05 "Fallout 4 loading screens"): _"Diamond City's newspaper, Publick Occurrences, gets its name from the first newspaper ever published in Boston, in 1690."_

15.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-21) The [Lone Wanderer](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Lone_Wanderer "Lone Wanderer"): _"What do you know about the Soil Stradivarius?"_  
    [Agatha](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Agatha "Agatha"): _"Not too much I'm afraid. It was fabricated way back in 1714 by a famous Italian craftsman named Antonio Stradivari. He had made a bunch of Stradivarius violins actually, and each one was individually named over time to identify them. They are regarded as the most outstanding instruments ever made... and no two sound alike they say. Incredible. Since the bombs fell laying waste to most of the world, it may be safe to say that this could be the last surviving violin of its kind."_  
    ([Agatha.txt](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Agatha.txt "Agatha.txt"))
16.  ↑ [16.0](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-OldNorthChurchInscription_22-0) [16.1](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-OldNorthChurchInscription_22-1) [Old North Church inscription](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Boston_landmark_inscriptions#Old_North_Church "Boston landmark inscriptions")
17.  ↑ [17.0](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-Trinity_Church_23-0) [17.1](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-Trinity_Church_23-1) _[Fallout 4 Vault Dweller's Survival Guide](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Fallout_4_Vault_Dweller%27s_Survival_Guide "Fallout 4 Vault Dweller's Survival Guide")_ Collector's Edition p.452: _"**\[11.02\] TRINITY PLAZA**_  
    _Still standing in the overgrown plaza that bears its name is Trinity Church. Founded in 1733, the present structure was completed in 1877 and now houses a small congregation of Super Mutants. The church has two entrances—the main doors and a hatch to the rear (east). Don’t forget the magazine from the pulpit. The area is easy to spot from a distance; it is adjacent to the massive Trinity Tower."_  
    ([Fallout 4 Vault Dweller's Survival Guide Map](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Fallout_4_Vault_Dweller%27s_Survival_Guide_Map "Fallout 4 Vault Dweller's Survival Guide Map"))
18.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-24) [Faneuil Hall terminal entries; manager's terminal, Tour Script](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Faneuil_Hall_terminal_entries#Tour_Script "Faneuil Hall terminal entries")

[↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-27) [Prickett's Fort curator](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Prickett%27s_Fort_curator "Prickett's Fort curator"): _"Another fascinating tidbit is that the fort didn't actually look like this. The builders of the fort used historical documentation that turned out to be almost pure fiction. So Prickett's Fort is technically a representational frontier fort. And thus the Revolutionary War began.Continue[![Image 1: In-game spelling, punctuation and/or grammar](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/fallout/images/3/3a/Icon_sic.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/16?cb=20110222202016)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sic "In-game spelling, punctuation and/or grammar") on the trail to walk through more of our great city's history."_

24.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-ButtonLeeResolution_32-0) [Lone Wanderer](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Lone_Wanderer "Lone Wanderer"): _"Is there anything else you can tell me about the Declaration?"_

    [Button Gwinnett](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Button_Gwinnett_/(robot/) "Button Gwinnett (robot)"): _"On July 4, 1776 the Second Continental Congress declared that the original Thirteen Colonies of America were now free and independent states.     ([Button Gwinnett's dialogue](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/MS15ButtonGwinnett.txt "MS15ButtonGwinnett.txt"))
26.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-34) [The End (episode)](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/The_End_/(episode/) "The End (episode)"), the [Vault 33](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Vault_33 "Vault 33") classroom shows 3 dates, 1776 (constitution), 1969 (new flag insignia), 2077 (thermonuclear mushroom cloud)
27.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-ButtonNewYork_35-0) [Lone Wanderer](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Lone_Wanderer "Lone Wanderer"): _"Any other facts you can share about the Declaration?"_

28.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-ButtonDelegatesSignatures_36-0) [Lone Wanderer](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Lone_Wanderer "Lone Wanderer"): _"What else do you know about the Declaration?"_  
    [Button Gwinnett](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Button_Gwinnett_/(robot/) "Button Gwinnett (robot)"): _"The Declaration of Independence wasn't fully signed by all of the delegates until August 2, 1776."_

    _The "New" State House was completed in 1798 to house the government of the state of Massachusetts. The land selected was originally one of John Hancock's cow pastures. The original dome was constructed of wooden shingles and covered in copper smelted by Paul Revere. The state government used this building continuously until the formation of the Thirteen Commonwealths in 1969."_

[↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-43) Labels on whiskey bottles in _[Fallout 4](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Fallout_4 "Fallout 4")_ and _[Fallout 76](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Fallout_76 "Fallout 76")_ ([image here](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/File:Fo4_Whiskey.png "File:Fo4 Whiskey.png"))

This experiment was influenced by Thoreau's interest in transcendentalist philosophy, which believed that people were at their best when truly self-reliant. For more information, please visit the gift shop and purchase one of the many books on transcendentalism. Also available; t-shirts, coffee mugs, toys, and many other items to commemorate your trip! Thank you for visiting Walden Pond, sponsored by General Atomics, maker of the Mister Handy robotic assistant."_

396.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-FO3OGGGYE_482-0) _[Fallout 3 Official Game Guide](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Fallout_3_Official_Game_Guide "Fallout 3 Official Game Guide")_ Game of the Year Edition p.42: _"**Super Mutants**"_  
    _"The Super Mutants that infest the urban ruin of Washington D.C. originated in Vault 87. Those unlucky enough to have reserved space in Vault 87 soon found themselves forcefully taken to a secure part of the Vault, where they were locked in airtight chambers and exposed to a concentrated form of the F.E.V. The Overseer and his security force had no real idea what to expect; they were simply following the "plan." When the exposed Vault dwellers started transforming into Super Mutants, nearly the entire Vault population had been exposed. Those who hadn't yet metamorphosed knew what was coming, and, well...it didn't end well for humanity._  
    _The dwellers of Vault 87 were turned into Super Mutants in 2078, and have been a presence in the Capital Wasteland ever since. Most of those original Super Mutants have long since been killed. But whether it's because of the nature of the F.E.V. they were exposed to, or a simple underlying human instinct, the Super Mutants of the Capital Wasteland are obsessed with the preservation of their own species. Super Mutants are asexual and incapable of procreation, so their only way of reproducing is to kidnap other humans, drag them back to the Vault 87 chambers, and infect them with F.E.V. And so they have done, for nearly 200 years. Super Mutant society is loosely hierarchical, with the weaker (most recently transformed) Super Mutants generally giving way to the stronger. The Super Mutant hierarchy, as defined by the Capital Wasteland contingent of the Brotherhood of Steel, is as follows: Grunt, Brute, Master, and Behemoth. Generally speaking, the Super Mutants of the Capital Wasteland get bigger, stronger, and dumber as they age. The Behemoths are so strong and savage that they’re the only thing feared by the other Super Mutants."_  
    ([Fallout 3 Official Game Guide faction profiles](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Fallout_3_Official_Game_Guide_faction_profiles "Fallout 3 Official Game Guide faction profiles"))

609.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-FO3_Guide_722-0) _[Fallout 3 Official Game Guide](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Fallout_3_Official_Game_Guide "Fallout 3 Official Game Guide")_ Game of the Year Edition p.42: _"**Vault Dwellers**_  
    _Vault 101 was actually part of an unscrupulous social experiment. All of the other Vaults were intended to be opened at one point or another when the "all clear" signal was sent from Vault-Tec or the appropriate regulatory agency, and this indeed, did transpire, with almost universally horrific results. But Vault 101's secret plans were different: The doors were never scheduled to open. Ever. In fact, the Vault was supplied with just the type of equipment it would need to keep functioning indefinitely-like spare parts for the water processor. But this was just the beginning:_  
    _The true experiment was even more devious and cunning. Although Vault 101 was about testing the human condition when a Vault never opened, this was only the first part of the plan. The "actual" experiment went far beyond that, and a select few knew the true nature; that this was to test the role of the Overseer. While the Overseer was able to interact (and even visit) the outside world via radio transmissions, and a secret tunnel from his sealed office, the rest of the inhabitants faced a much more dismal future: As far as they knew, Vault 101 was never sent an "all clear" signal, and faked radio transmissions described a nuclear-ravaged world gone mad, with absolutely no hope of existence outside of a Vault. The radio transmissions were actually recorded before the bombs even fell, and in many cases described a world even more horrible than the reality of the nuclear wasteland. The Vault 101 Overseer, like his counterparts in the other Vaults, was actually a planted Vault-Tec operative whose job it was to control the experiment from the inside._  
    _Aside from keeping up this ruse, the Overseer's other important role was to reinforce to the dwellers of Vault 101 that the outside world would never be habitable again, and that their only salvation was in the Vault. The Overseer prevented anyone from leaving the Vault, and made sure the Vault dwellers received their regular "transmission" from the outside world. People entered Vault 101 in 2077, just before the bombs fell._  
    _The Overseer died of natural causes 50 years later (in 2127), at the age of 84, after grooming a subordinate to continue the clandestine plan. The new Overseer led his people according to the same isolationist doctrine preached by his predecessor, but also attempted to garner as many senior Vault Dwellers to become complicit in this plan as possible. By 2277, the descendants of the Overseer had an entire generation of Vault Dwellers who were playing along with this plan, keeping the secrets from their children._  
    _The Overseer and his cronies continued to receive periodic information from the outside world, while those not in the know were told that things had gotten so bad that whoever was sending transmissions was no longer able to do so; reinforcing the thought that leaving the Vault was sheer suicide. The final piece of this grand experiment only truly began when the Vault Dwellers living in blissful ignorance finally realized the world outside could be accessed, and there was a possibility of life above ground. The experiment only really commenced when the Vault 101 door first opened, and a young dweller fled into the light."_  
    ([Fallout 3 Official Game Guide faction profiles](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Fallout_3_Official_Game_Guide_faction_profiles "Fallout 3 Official Game Guide faction profiles"))

    2196 _Tandi (Aradesh's daughter) is unanimously elected President by the NCR council. Her popularity is to prove enduring: she will continue to serve in office until her death in 2248, at the age of 103._  
    2242-2243 _The events of Fallout 2 take place._

    2273 _Aaron Kimball retires from the NCR military and runs for office as one of Hub's political representatives (or "governors," as Hub idiosyncratically calls them).     _The New California Republic was born from the remnants of the survivors of Vault 15 and the small walled community they founded, Shady Sands. Under the leadership of Aradesh, and with the assistance of the Vault Dweller (who saved Tandi, Aradesh's daughter and a future president of the NCR), the community prospered. Trade routes with other settlements allowed cultural exchange, and a movement to form a national entity gradually took root and won popular acceptance. In 2186, the town of Shady Sands changed its name to "New California Republic" and formed a trial council government to draft a constitution. Four more settlements joined the council, and in 2189 the NCR was voted into existence as a sprawling federation of five states: Shady Sands, Los Angeles, Maxson, Hub, and Dayglow._  
    _By post-apocalyptic standards, the NCR is a paragon of economic success and good ethical character: political enfranchisement, rule of law, a reasonable degree of physical security, and a standard of living better than mere subsistence are daily realities for it's 700,000+ citizens. Currently, the NCR in a state of transition, with rapid economic growth and a sea change in political leadership endangering its grand humanitarian ideals. Nowhere is this more evident than in the Mojave, where the occupation of Hoover Dam has improved access to electricity and water, but at the cost of straining its budget and embroiling its armed forces in a morally corrosive imperialist project._  
    _The NCR government's aim is to annex New Vegas as the republic's sixth state. While it already controls Hoover Dam, its treaty with Mr. House and the three families compels it to allot one-fifth of the dam's electrical and water production to local use free of charge. Adding injury to insult, the NCR is locked into protecting New Vegas from invasion by Caesar's legion even as it receives not one cap in tax revenue from the Strip's highly lucrative resort operations. NCR citizens in the Mojave have largely come here for economic reasons, whether as paid citizen soldiers or as prospectors and fortune-seekers."_

That was back in '73, if I recall. Lot of those Rangers are dead now. Vegas always chewed men up... it's just a little more literal, nowadays."_  
    ([Corporal Sterling's dialogue](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/1ECorporalSterling.txt "1ECorporalSterling.txt"))
724.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-906) The [Courier](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Courier "Courier"): _"Why did you leave the Rangers?"_  
    [Sterling](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Sterling_/(Fallout:_New_Vegas/) "Sterling (Fallout: New Vegas)"): _"Well... that wasn't really a matter of choice. Got myself caught by Legionnaires, up near Malpais. They had themselves some fun with me... mangled my hands and feet pretty good. Wasn't much good with a pistol after that. Wasn't gonna be trekking across the waste on any more long scouts, either."_  
    ([Corporal Sterling's dialogue](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/1ECorporalSterling.txt "1ECorporalSterling.txt"))
725.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-907) The [Courier](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Courier "Courier"): _"How did you manage to escape Malpais?"_  
    [Sterling](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Sterling_/(Fallout:_New_Vegas/) "Sterling (Fallout: New Vegas)"): _"Caesar's boys figured I wasn't going anywhere, after what they done to me. So they didn't bother tying me up. I crawled out of there on my elbows and knees. Must have looked a sight. Then I rolled down an embankment into the Colorado. Guess I had a mind to drown, rather than give Caesar's boys the satisfaction of killing me. But a couple Rangers happened to be watching from across the river. They jumped on in and pulled me out of there. Lucky break, they said."_  
    ([Corporal Sterling's dialogue](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/1ECorporalSterling.txt "1ECorporalSterling.txt"))
726.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-908) The [Courier](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Courier "Courier"): _"What are your plans for New Vegas?"_  
    [Robert House](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Robert_House "Robert House"): _"I've resurrected Vegas, spirit intact. What I need now is the ability to enforce my rightful claim. Not just against Caesar's Legion, by the way. In fact, the NCR is a more present and insidious threat."_  
    The Courier: _"How do you intend to enforce your claim on the city?"_  
    Robert House: _"To enforce, one must have force - a position of strength. Years ago, when I detected NCR scouts roaming the Mojave, I could tell from their uniforms that these were no mere tribesmen. I knew it was only a matter of time before an army appeared, to take control of the dam. And I knew my Securitrons wouldn't be enough to oppose them. And so I recruited the Three Families. Vegas belongs to me because I mustered enough strength to bring the NCR to the bargaining table."_  
    ([Robert House's dialogue](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/MrHouse.txt "MrHouse.txt"))
727.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-909) The [Courier](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Courier "Courier"): _"How long were you the head of the family?"_  
    [Benny](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Benny "Benny"): _"Seven years. Took over three days after Mr. House introduced himself. Our chief at the time, mountain of a guy named Bingo, wanted to stay nomadic. I disagreed, so he challenged me to the knife. He looked so surprised when I stuck that knife in his neck. Thought he was so tough, but he was so slow. That's how I made chief. It's how things were back then."_  
    ([Benny's dialogue](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Benny.txt "Benny.txt"))
728.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-910) The [Courier](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Courier "Courier"): _"What was your relationship with Benny... back when he was breathing?"_  
    [Robert House](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Robert_House "Robert House"): _"Benny was the leader of the Chairmen for seven years, ever since I recruited the tribe. I considered him something of a protege."_  
    ([Robert House's dialogue](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/MrHouse.txt "MrHouse.txt"))
729.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-911) The [Courier](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Courier "Courier"): _"Why do you care whether Kimball lives or dies?"_  
    [Robert House](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Robert_House "Robert House"): _"I care because he is a known quantity - not the man so much as the political context he inhabits. Kimball rose to prominence as the "Hero of the Mojave" when he led a campaign of reprisals against tribals who dared to attack NCR citizens. Ordering the occupation of Hoover Dam was his first act of office. As water and electricity flowed to NCR cities, his popularity soared. Conversely, his failure to annex the Mojave these seven years, and the immense costs of occupying a foreign land, have eroded his popular support."_  
    ([Robert House's dialogue](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/MrHouse.txt "MrHouse.txt"))
730.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-912) The [Courier](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Courier "Courier"): _"Wasn't the NCR's army big enough to defeat your Securitrons and the Three Families?"_  
    [Robert House](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Robert_House "Robert House"): _"Indeed it was - and still is. But not without taking significant casualties. Would Kimball and Oliver have traded the lives of hundreds of soldiers for absolute control of Hoover Dam? Oh yes. They weren't afraid of me, they were afraid of Caesar - that attacking me would leave them vulnerable to a Legion offensive. And so they negotiated. Not out of the kindness of their hearts, as they try to make it seem. Because the calculus of power left no other choice."_  
    ([Robert House's dialogue](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/MrHouse.txt "MrHouse.txt"))
731.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-913) The [Courier](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Courier "Courier"): _"What were the terms of your treaty with the NCR?"_  
    [Robert House](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Robert_House "Robert House"): _"NCR forces were permitted to occupy Hoover Dam and establish a military base at McCarran Airport. Well, it used to be one. They recognized my sovereignty over the Vegas Strip and agreed to supply electricity and water once their engineers repaired the dam. Written into the treaty were provisions that the NCR do nothing to prevent its soldiers and civilians from visiting the Strip. That's how I harnessed the NCR to my endeavor. Their occupation has been the engine of my growing economy."_  
    ([Robert House's dialogue](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/MrHouse.txt "MrHouse.txt"))
732.  ↑ [733.0](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-crocker_history_lesson_914-0) [733.1](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-crocker_history_lesson_914-1) The [Courier](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Courier "Courier"): _"I'd like to know more about the NCR."_  
    [Dennis Crocker](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Dennis_Crocker "Dennis Crocker"): _"I can provide a quick history lesson, if that's what you're looking for. In 2274, President Kimball sent the NCR army into the Mojave in force, with the objective of occupying and repairing Hoover Dam. Rangers and army scouts had confirmed that the dam was basically unoccupied and could be restored to an operable condition. Upon arriving at the dam, however, they discovered that a large force of tribals and robots had occupied it. This was our introduction to the Three Families, the Securitrons, and, of course, Mr. House. Using his Securitrons as intermediaries, Mr. House called for parlay. He claimed his forces had occupied Hoover Dam in order to safeguard it for our arrival. And that he was ready to turn it over to us, so long as we could agree to terms. Those terms became the Treaty of New Vegas. The Treaty recognized Mr. House's sovereignty over the Strip and granted us rights to establish military bases at the Dam and McCarran Airport. The NCR is legally permitted to send 95% of the electricity produced by the dam to our home states. The remaining 5% goes to the Strip. The treaty actually makes it illegal for the NCR to prevent its citizens, or troops on furlough, from visiting the Strip. Once on the Strip, our citizens are subject to arrest - or punishment - by House's Securitrons, though that's a rare occurrence. Our troops enjoy a different status. It's illegal for the Securitrons to take action against them. Of course, it's also illegal for our troops to carry firearms on the Strip, so there isn't much trouble they can get into. Our military police does an adequate job of keeping the troops on furlough in line. I don't envy them that task. The embassy was established a few weeks after the Treaty was signed. Basically Mr. House handed us a dumpy little building he had no interest in renovating. I'm the third ambassador to hold this post. And the first, I think, to accept its limitations. My predecessors had ambitions of engineering the annexation of the Mojave. They thought they'd convince Mr. House to join up. I've never even spoken to the man - or whatever he is. Maybe the situation will change once we've beaten the Legion once and for all."_  
    The Courier: _"Go on."_  
    Dennis Crocker: _"Now we mostly just keep track of the NCR citizens and troopers around and make sure they don't get in trouble, but that's Captain Pappas' job. I keep myself busy with paperwork and reports that get sent back to the NCR. It's mostly busy work, but every once in awhile, we make progress."_  
    ([Ambassador Crocker's dialogue](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/VStreetDennisCrocker.txt "VStreetDennisCrocker.txt"))
733.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-915) The [Courier](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Courier "Courier"): _"How long has he been in Goodsprings?"_  
    Trudy: _"It was here when I took over the saloon seven years ago. Some people have said its owner lived here, but no one knows who it was."_  
    ([Trudy's dialogue](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Trudy%27s_dialogue "Trudy's dialogue"))
734.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-916) The [Lone Wanderer](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Lone_Wanderer "Lone Wanderer"): _"How did you get to be in charge of this place?"_  
    [Robert MacCready](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Robert_MacCready "Robert MacCready"): _"It's not that complex. Any kid can say they want to be mayor here. It's just that most don't want to bother with the responsibility of leading. Most of the time, they last until the kids get tired of them, then they get kicked out on their ass by the new mayor. One only lasted 5 minutes. Of course, I've kept this place going strong for three years. To most of these kids, that makes me Mayor For Fucking Life. Fine by me, I say."_  
    ([Mayor MacCready's dialogue in _Fallout 3_](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/MayorMacCready.txt "MayorMacCready.txt"))
735.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-918) [PIP-Boy 3000 date](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/File:Fo3_FI_Date.png "File:Fo3 FI Date.png") during the [Future Imperfect](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Future_Imperfect "Future Imperfect") quest.
736.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-919) The [Lone Wanderer](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Lone_Wanderer "Lone Wanderer"): _"I'm sorry... Who's Maggie?"_

737.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-920) The [Courier](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Courier "Courier"): _"Where does New Vegas get all its electricity?"_

    ([Robert House's dialogue](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/MrHouse.txt "MrHouse.txt"))

740.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-923) The [Lone Wanderer](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Lone_Wanderer "Lone Wanderer"): _"Tell me more about the Outcasts."_

741.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-924) _[Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Fallout:_New_Vegas_Official_Game_Guide "Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide")_ Collector's Edition p.42: _"**Freeside**_  
    _Las Vegas wasn't heavily damaged during the Great War, but people didn't immediately "settle" into the remnants of the old city. The various Vault tribes that emerged years later, hunted and fought among the ruins, but it was not until the "return" of Mr. House that they ceased (most) of their hostilities. Mr House directed the tribes to use his sizable quantities of pre-war construction materials to build the crude (but effective) outer walls that separate The Strip and Freeside from the rest of New Vegas. While Mr. House valued the area around Fremont Street, he ultimately viewed it as secondary in importance to the Strip itself and he had a second, inner wall that separated the two areas. When NCR prospectors (and eventually the army) arrived in the region, people typically went straight for The Strip, leaving Freeside (as it had become known by locals) as an informal stopping point. Eventually Mr. House recognized that he could use Freeside as a filter for undesirables, and pulled his favored tribes and all Securitrons into the Strip, leaving Freeside to fend for itself._  
    _In the two years that followed, Freeside has slowly degenerated into a hostile, lawless den of ne'er-do-wells. For a while, it was completely without order, but two power groups managed to come to an understanding about how the area needed to be maintained. The Kings, formed from the dispossessed remnants of unfortunate tribes, prevent all-out chaos from erupting, but do little to deal with the day-to-day nastiness that Freesiders inflict on each other. The Followers of the Apocalypse, no longer associated with the NCR, settled in the Old Mormon Fort. They receive some protection from the Kings in exchange for help with the community's basic needs (food, water, health services, and some education). Despite the oversight from the Kings and help from the Followers, the people in Freeside live in daily peril... from each other as well as outside forces."_  
    ([Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide faction profiles](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Fallout:_New_Vegas_Official_Game_Guide_faction_profiles "Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide faction profiles"))
742.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-925) The [Courier](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Courier "Courier"): _"Tell me about the Kings."_  
    [Gloria Van Graff](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Gloria_Van_Graff "Gloria Van Graff"): _"Ah, the "rulers" of Freeside. The Kings are a bunch of boys who refuse to grow up, and this is their playground. Their leader seems different, though. The few times I've dealt with him I've been impressed despite myself. When we first arrived in Freeside, the Kings protested when we kicked out the original occupant of this establishment. 743.  [↑](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline#cite_ref-926) The [Courier](https://fallout.fandom.com/wiki/Courier "Courier"): _"Yes, what is the task?"_

    Much of modern-day Boston's skyline consists of buildings that were constructed well after Fallout's timeline diverged from our own. The taller structures that make the city recognizable are too contemporary in their designs. That gave us a blank slate to work with in terms of designing our version of a city of tomorrow. The older historical aspects of the city were retained for authenticity, but we wanted to layer them with some futuristic architecture, as this is a type of environment that hasn't been explored yet in the Fallout universe. As you can see in these early concepts, we explored some pretty far-out ideas for just how built up and evolved our version of Boston would be.     _The NCR's economy is based on two resources: its great Brahmin herds, and swaths of land that have been restored to arable condition. This has given birth to a number of cottage industries, from the rebirth of luxury goods production to "journalism" that reports on the latest purchases, commissions, and "life lessons" of the newly rich and famous._

Citizens of the NCR rarely face significant dangers on a daily basis, and survival is an assumption rather than an aspiration.     _A consequence of these economic and cultural transformations has been the rebirth of wage labor. To earn their keep, many citizens must seek an employer and trade the sweat of their brow for Caps._

Many curse the selfishness of their fellow citizens, usually while pursuing aims that will benefit only themselves or their families. Here in the Vegas wastes, however, nearly all citizens will agree on one matter: opportunity has dried up back home, and to earn a fortune, one must come East."_
